t: Nothing of the church remains here now. This spot is occupied by Number 1 Poultry, but it was once the site of St Benet Sherehog, a medieval parish church built before the year 1111, in the City's wool-dealing district. A shere hog is a castrated ram after its first shearing. Several people were buried here, including two Lord Mayors, Sir Ralph Warren and Sir John Lyon. The astronomer and antiquarian John Greaves lies here too, and so does the poet Katherine Philips, known as the Matchless Orinda, whom Dryden and Keats both admired.
